page: Microsoft Azure D16pls_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine within the general-purpose Dplsv7 series, configured with a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on an arm64 processor architecture running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 16 dedicated virtual cores paired with 32.0 GB of system memory. This establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance (2.0 GB per vCPU), which shifts the resource profile toward compute-intensive execution compared to standard 1:4 general-purpose instances.

Hardware capabilities do not include local disk storage or onboard graphics processing units. Storage operations rely entirely on remote managed volumes via Azure Premium Storage capabilities. The architecture provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard Azure virtual networking constructs for external routing. By pairing dedicated ARM64 compute capacity with a lean memory footprint, the configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for scaled multi-threaded operations that do not demand extensive in-memory working sets.

The primary tradeoff of the D16pls_v7 instance involves its memory density and lack of ephemeral local scratch space. Workloads requiring high memory caching or fast temporary NVMe storage must accommodate the 32.0 GB ceiling and depend on network-attached storage throughput. Consequently, the instance is targeted at scaled web serving tiers, application gateways, containerized microservices, distributed CI/CD build agents, and parallel compute tasks optimized for ARM instruction sets.
description: Microsoft Azure D16pls_v7 is an arm64 virtual machine instance offering 16 dedicated virtual cores and 32.0 GB of system memory, managed through the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Characterized by its low-memory 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio providing 2.0 GB per vCPU, the instance is designed to prioritize multi-core computational throughput over heavy in-memory data storage. The instance includes no onboard graphics processors and features no local ephemeral storage, directing all disk input and output to remote Premium Storage subsystems. This architectural layout delivers an efficient resource profile for CPU-driven multi-threaded workloads on ARM architecture without incurring costs for unneeded memory allocation. The server is suited for containerized services, microservice middle-tiers, distributed build automation, batch computing, and horizontal web application serving.
